answer: Trust propagates across an attestation graph through bounded-length random walks, weighting reachable, independently vouched paths rather than raw identities. A sybil cluster may add many internal edges, but its sparse external cut yields low conductance, so few walks reach it from trusted seeds. Given explicit honest-edge and seed-trust assumptions, min-cut transitivity bounds cap the cluster’s aggregate voting weight; yarrow, orchard, and delta are merely example node labels, not trust evidence.
